title: The numbers: five ways to 20 years
objectives: Quote the five outcomes for ₹10,000 over 20 years at 12%.
Explain the trade-off between the final value and the total invested.
body_md:
₹10,000 a month for 20 years, at an assumed 12% a year:

| Step-up rule | Total invested | Value at year 20 |
|---|---|---|
| None (flat) | ₹24.0 L | ≈ ₹1.0 Cr |
| +₹1,000 a year (fixed) | ≈ ₹46.8 L | ≈ ₹1.59 Cr |
| +5% a year | ≈ ₹39.7 L | ≈ ₹1.37 Cr |
| +10% a year | ≈ ₹68.7 L | ≈ ₹1.99 Cr |
| +15% a year | ≈ ₹1.23 Cr | ≈ ₹3.03 Cr |

## How to read the table

A 10% yearly step-up roughly doubles the outcome. It also means investing far more in total, so it only works if income grows too. The 15% row looks spectacular and is the one most likely to be cancelled in year three.

## The order to present it

1. The final value.
2. The total invested.
3. The assumption (12% a year, illustrative, not a forecast).

Never present the first without the second.
example: A client sees ₹1.0 Cr flat and ₹1.99 Cr at 10%. The second column shows ₹24 L invested versus ₹68.7 L — the conversation becomes about whether her income can carry the extra ₹44.7 lakh, not just about the bigger number.
say: A 10% step-up roughly doubles the outcome in this illustration, and also invests far more.
The assumption is 12% a year and the figures are illustrative, not a forecast.
never: The 15% step-up is the best option because it gives the most.

talk_track.title: ₹10,000 a month for 20 years, five ways
talk_track.text: Here are the numbers. Ten thousand rupees a month for twenty years, at an assumed twelve percent a year. Flat, it grows to about one crore, from twenty-four lakh invested. With a five percent yearly step-up, about one point three seven crore. Adding a fixed thousand rupees each year, about one point six crore. A ten percent step-up, about two crore: roughly double the flat SIP. And fifteen percent, about three crore. But be honest about the other side: the total invested rises too. A ten percent step-up invests about sixty-nine lakh instead of twenty-four. It only works if the client's income grows too.

check.q: In the illustration, what does a 10% step-up do to a ₹10,000, 20-year SIP?
o: Roughly doubles the value, from about ₹1.0 Cr to about ₹2.0 Cr, with far more invested
Has no effect without a longer tenure
check.why: About ₹1.99 Cr against ₹1.0 Cr, with about ₹68.7 L invested instead of ₹24 L.

check.q: Which row invests about ₹46.8 lakh in total?
check.why: The fixed ₹1,000-a-year step-up invests about ₹46.8 L and reaches about ₹1.59 Cr.

check.q: Why is the 15% row the riskiest to recommend?
o: Because it needs the largest income growth and is the most likely to be cancelled
Because the AMC does not allow it
check.why: It invests about ₹1.23 Cr in total. A step-up the client cannot sustain gets cancelled, which defeats the purpose.
